sections.title: Close-up - grapes growing on a vine
sections.description: The curved woody vine joins leaf petioles and hanging fruit stalks. Grape leaves have a basal sinus and radiating palmate veins; only selected leaves have folds.

sections.title: Close-up - naturally layered oak and angled acorns
sections.description: White-oak leaves spread forward, backward and sideways from connected twigs. Selected foreground leaves partly cover the acorns; other acorns remain unobscured by those leaves.

sections.title: Close-up - leafy juniper branch and berries
sections.description: Berry pedicels and whorled needle sprays grow from the same woody juniper branch; this plant is not a vine.

sections.title: Close-up - corn with raised kernels and peeled husks
sections.description: Kernels project beyond a narrow inner cob. Curved crowns, visible side walls and short underside hatching describe relief; the kernel contours themselves make the uneven outer edge. Two distinct ear angles sit among fuller rye fans.

sections.title: Detail - raised corn kernels and side faces
sections.description: A tighter view of the first ear shows the rounded kernel crowns, shaded lower side walls and projecting edge kernels. The smooth inner cob is beneath the kernel layer, not the outer silhouette.

sections.title: Transition - grape vine into hops and barley
sections.description: A smaller late grape bunch and palmate leaves overlap the first hop leaves and barley stalks, rather than stopping at a sharp boundary.

sections.title: Transition - hops and barley into juniper
sections.description: A smaller hop leaf and cone extend among progressively fuller juniper sprays. Every plant retains its own connected support.

sections.title: Transition - juniper into rye
sections.description: Juniper needles taper down in size while early rye heads and leaves emerge among the ending sprays.

sections.title: Transition - rye into white oak
sections.description: The first oak leaves are smaller; late rye stalks extend behind the growing oak leaf masses and their connected fruit twigs.

sections.title: Wine - grapes and leaves on a flowing vine
sections.description: A woody grape vine connects alternating petioles, palmate serrated leaves, curled tendrils and hanging grape bunches. Short visible shoots explain the growth between overlaps.

sections.title: Beer - hops on bines and barley stalks
sections.description: Hop leaves and cones attach to a fine twining bine concealed beneath the foliage. Barley heads retain their shape and grow on their own slender culms, not a shared vine.

sections.title: Gin - juniper berries on leafy branches
sections.description: Common juniper is woody, not a vine. Needle-bearing side shoots and berry pedicels join a tapered branch mostly hidden among the dense sprays.

sections.title: Whiskey / bourbon - rye stalks and husked corn
sections.description: Small rye fans enrich the individual stalks without changing the grain-head anatomy. Differently angled corn ears have raised kernel crowns, shaded side faces and an uneven kernel-built silhouette, with partially peeled husks.

sections.title: White oak - layered leaves and angled acorns
sections.description: Quercus alba leaves spread at varied angles from woody twigs. Some foreground leaves partially conceal the angled acorns, while other acorns remain unobscured by foreground leaves. Smaller first leaves overlap the fading rye stalks.
